title: Approve the quieter Noir composition
question: Quiet Signal removes the ambient bar field and alternating bands, leaving the terminal as the single bold anchor. Which balance should carry into the implementation?

options.label: Quiet Signal
options.lineage: the Luminous Index reduced to one signal and one proof surface
options.thesis: A calm documentation sheet explains Noir first; a single exact terminal frame supplies the contrast and character.
options.viewport: A spacious promise, install command, and first action lead into one terminal specimen; the architecture path becomes a secondary cue and the next fold opens as three quiet links.
options.risk: Its restraint depends on typography and spacing being executed precisely; weak type choices would make it merely minimal.

options.label: Luminous Index
options.lineage: a white technical index with the full data vocabulary visible
options.thesis: Signal bars, architecture trace, terminal proof, and alternating guide rows all share the first viewport.
options.viewport: A white editorial field holds the quick start while a tall black terminal anchors the right edge and a data stream hangs from the navigation.
options.risk: Distinctive, but too many simultaneous motifs make a reading surface feel active before the visitor begins reading.

options.label: Split Signal
options.lineage: a hard source/output seam joined by one retained signal
options.thesis: Live terminal output and explanation receive equal visual authority across a hard black-and-white split.
options.viewport: A black terminal fills the left side; the right side carries the promise and actions; one labeled pipeline crosses the seam.
options.risk: The split is memorable but carries too much visual weight for long-form documentation and makes every page want to become a poster.
